### `TulaCeremony`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Ceremony.kt`

How something the system showed the user ended: it gave an answer, or the user put it away.

**A dismissed sheet is not an error and not a success.** Nothing was sent to prove
anything, nobody is signed in, and the same call works again: an app goes back to where it
was and says nothing, or says so in a neutral tone.

### `BrowserReturn`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Ceremony.kt`

The wait of a [BrowserSession] for the address its app is opened with, kept apart from the
platform so that which address ends the wait is tested on a JVM.

An app is opened with whatever matches its intent filter, and anybody can open an app with
a URL: an address is taken for the browser's return only when it is the redirect URL the
sign-in asked for, character for character, followed by `#`. Any other address is the
app's own and leaves the wait as it was. The client still reads the whole address by the
same rule; this is what keeps a stray deep link from ending a sign-in that is under way.

```kotlin
class BrowserReturn
```

_fun_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Ceremony.kt`

The client's word for a credential sheet's failure.

Only the platform's own cancellation is a dismissal. A `NotAllowedError` is a failure: a

would report a refused ceremony as "the user put it away".

### `DeviceKeyStore`

_interface_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/DeviceKey.kt`

Where the client's device key is kept.

**"There is no key" and "the key could not be had" are different answers, and the client
acts on the difference.** [existing] returns `null` only when the store knows there is no
key: a bound session whose key is gone is over, and the client ends it. It throws when it
cannot tell (a locked device, a store that failed): the client reports `device.key_failed`
and keeps the session, because the same call may work a moment later. Never answer `null`
for a failure, and never throw for a key that is simply not there.

```kotlin
interface DeviceKeyStore
```

_fun_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/DeviceKey.kt`

The key of this app on this device, or `null` when there is none.

@throws Exception when the store cannot say whether there is a key, or cannot hand it

_fun_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/DeviceKey.kt`

Make the key and keep it. Called only after [existing] answered `null`; a store that
finds a key was made meanwhile returns that one.

**It may be called while an earlier call is still out.** The client asks one thing at a
time, but a removal drops the calls from before it, and a call that does not end when
it is cancelled can still be running when the next one starts. A store must tolerate
two at once and end with one key.

#### `DeviceKeyStore.remove`

_fun_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/DeviceKey.kt`

Remove what is kept of the key; nothing there is not an error.

The client calls it by itself in one case: at a sign-out, when [existing] threw
[DeviceKeyUnusableException]. For every other failure it is **not** called: the failure
may pass, and two clients that share one store share its key. An app that knows better
than the store removes the key itself, after a sign-out, **through
[TulaClient.removeDeviceKey]**, which calls this and tells the client.

```kotlin
suspend fun remove()
```

```kotlin
    val field: String,
    /** The problem's code, e.g. `password.too_short`. */
    val code: String,
    /** A message for the user, from the client's message table. */

)
```

### `TulaError`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Errors.kt`

The one error every failed call of the client throws.

[code] is a contract code (`auth.invalid_credentials`, `password.too_short`,
`rate_limited`, …) or one of [ClientErrorCodes]. [message] is ready to show. An error never
holds a token, an attempt's secret, a password or a code.

**It keeps nothing of what the platform threw**: no cause, no suppressed exception, none of
its text. An engine's or a key store's exception names what it was doing (a request's
address holds an attempt's id), and Android writes an exception to the log with its whole
chain. What failed is the [code]; why, in the platform's words, is not kept anywhere.

```kotlin
class TulaError(
    /** A contract error code, or one of the client's own. */
    val code: String,
    message: String,
    /** HTTP status of the API's answer; `0` when the request got none. */
    val status: Int = 0,
    /** Values that give the error its specifics, e.g. `min` → `10`. */
    val params: Map<String, Any> = emptyMap(),
    /** Field-level problems (`validation.failed`, password rules). Empty when there are none. */
    val errors: List<TulaFieldError> = emptyList(),
    /**
     * How long to wait before trying again, in milliseconds, when the server said
     * (`Retry-After`). The client never waits or retries for it by itself.
     */
    val retryAfterMs: Long? = null,
) : Exception(message)
```

`sms_code`), in its order. Empty for any other error.


### `Flow`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Flows.kt`

A flow in progress: a sign-up, a sign-in or a password reset. [step] says what the server is
waiting for; each action sends one request and returns the next step. When the step is
`complete` the client is signed in.

A flow sends one action at a time. A second action while one is in flight is refused with
`flow.busy`, and any action once the flow has completed or was discarded with
`flow.invalid_step`; both are raised by the client (status `0`) without a request.

The attempt's secret is held in this object's private state, in memory, until the flow
completes or is discarded. It is not a property, is never written to storage, and is in no
[toString], error or snapshot.

```kotlin
abstract class Flow internal constructor(
    private val context: FlowContext,
    started: FlowAttempt,
    private val operations: FlowOperations,
)
```

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Http.kt`

### `UrlConnectionEngine`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Http.kt`

The default [HttpEngine]: `java.net.HttpURLConnection`, which the JVM and every Android
version have, so the client adds no HTTP dependency to an app.

Each request runs on a thread of the engine's own pool and is given up (the connection is
closed) when the calling coroutine is cancelled, which is how the client's timeout ends it.
Redirects are not followed, nothing is cached and no cookie is kept.

`HttpURLConnection` has no `PATCH`; the client's calls do not need one today.

**It was tested on a desktop JVM only.** Android's `HttpURLConnection` is another
implementation, and the API refuses a sign-in and ends a session with a `401` that has no
`WWW-Authenticate` header: that Android hands over such an answer's status and body was
not tried on a device. An app that does not want to rest on it passes an [HttpEngine] of
its own (over OkHttp, for one).

```kotlin
class UrlConnectionEngine : HttpEngine
```

### `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRY_SKEW_MS`

_val_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Session.kt`

How long before an access token expires the client stops using it and refreshes instead.

A token has to outlive the request that carries it: the time to reach the API plus any
difference between clocks. For a shorter-lived token the skew is capped at half its lifetime.

```kotlin
const val ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRY_SKEW_MS: Long = 10_000
```

### `REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS`

_val_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Session.kt`

How long a refresh request may take before it fails with `network.timeout`, unless the client
was created with a smaller timeout.

It is deliberately shorter than the server's smallest refresh reuse grace period (10
seconds). A refresh whose answer is lost may already have rotated the token on the server;
presenting the same token again is forgiven only inside the grace period, and treated as
theft (the whole session is revoked) after it. The same number as `@tula/core`'s
`REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS`; a test of the repository holds the two equal.

```kotlin
const val REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS: Long = 8_000
```

### `REFRESH_RETRY_WINDOW_MS`

_val_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Session.kt`

How long, from the start of a refresh, its one automatic repeat may still be running: the
server's default refresh reuse grace period.

A refresh that gets no answer (a timeout or a network failure, never an HTTP answer) is sent
once more, at once. It is the only request the client repeats by itself, and it is safe by
design: if the server did rotate the token, it answers the same token presented again inside
the grace period with the same next token.

```kotlin
const val REFRESH_RETRY_WINDOW_MS: Long = 10_000
```

### `MAX_REFRESH_BACKOFF_MS`

_val_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Session.kt`

The longest a `Retry-After` on a failed refresh makes [TulaSession.getToken] fail fast
without asking again. An explicit [TulaSession.refresh] always asks.

```kotlin
const val MAX_REFRESH_BACKOFF_MS: Long = 5 * 60_000
```

### `TokenStorage`

_interface_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Storage.kt`

Where the client keeps its refresh token between runs of the app.

The refresh token is a long-lived credential. On a device, back this with the platform's
secure store: `KeystoreTokenStorage` of the `tula-auth-android` module. Never plain
`SharedPreferences`, a file or a database.

A storage that fails **throws**; it never answers `null` for a read that could not be made.
`null` means "there is no token", and the client signs out on it. On a throw the client
reports `storage.failed` and keeps the session it has.

### `SealedTokenStorage`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Storage.kt`

A [TokenStorage] that writes nothing but sealed values: what reaches [entries] is
`base64(seal(value))`, with the entry's name bound in, so a sealed token cannot be moved
under another name.

A value that can never be opened ([ValueSealer.open] answers `null`: no key, or bytes the
sealer did not write; or the entry is not base64 and so not this storage's writing) is
removed and read as "no token". Every other failure is thrown, nothing is removed, and the
client keeps the session: a value whose authentication tag fails while the key exists is
one of those. Such an entry goes when the user signs out or signs in again: [remove] and
[set] never open what is stored.

The sealer and the entries may block (a Keystore operation, a write to disk): every call
runs on `Dispatchers.IO`, **one at a time**: a read that removes an entry it could not
open is a read and then a removal, and a token written between the two would be removed
with it. Two storages over the same entries do not share the lock: one per file.

```kotlin
class SealedTokenStorage(
    private val sealer: ValueSealer,
    private val entries: SealedEntries,
) : TokenStorage
```

### `AesGcmSealer`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/Storage.kt`

A [ValueSealer] over one AES-GCM key. A sealed value is `version, nonce length, nonce,
ciphertext and tag`; the context is the additional authenticated data.

What [open] answers for a value it cannot open is decided here, for every key store:

- bytes this sealer did not write (another format, another nonce length, cut short) and
  **no key** are `null`: the value can never be opened;
- **a tag that fails while the key exists is thrown** ([javax.crypto.AEADBadTagException]),
  like every other failure of the key store. A key store that answers wrongly once must
  not cost the user their session, and nothing here can tell that from an entry that was
  altered.

**A key that cannot be had is replaced when a value is sealed, and never when one is
opened.** Sealing writes the only value kept under the key, so a key the store can no
longer load (or that no longer takes an encryption) is removed and made again
([SealingKeys.replace]): otherwise no sign-in on the device could keep its session again.
Opening never replaces and never deletes: a store that fails now may answer later, and the
value it would open is a session. The cost of a replacement is the value sealed before it:
if the write that follows fails, that entry's tag fails until a later write or a sign-out.

@param keys Where the key is: the Android Keystore on a device, memory in a test.

```kotlin
class AesGcmSealer(private val keys: SealingKeys) : ValueSealer
```

### `TulaClient`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/TulaClient.kt`

The Tula Auth client for Android and the JVM: flows, the session and its refresh. It has no
UI and no Android dependency.

```kotlin
val tula = TulaClient(
    publishableKey = "tula_pk_…",
    baseUrl = "https://auth.example.com",
    storage = KeystoreTokenStorage(context),
)
tula.load()                                   // signed in from a stored session, or not
val flow = tula.signIn(identifier = email)
flow.submitPassword(password)                 // tula.state.value is AuthState.SignedIn
val token = tula.session.getToken()           // for the app's own backend
```

One client per API and environment for the life of the process: two clients over one storage
would each refresh the same token.

@param publishableKey The environment's publishable key (`tula_pk_…`). Never a secret key.
@param baseUrl The API's address, `https://…`; plain `http` is for a development server.
@param storage Where the refresh token is kept. There is no default on purpose: on a device
  it is `KeystoreTokenStorage`, and [MemoryTokenStorage] is a decision to forget the session
  when the process ends.
@param http How requests are sent.
@param clock The time.
@param timeoutMs How long one request may take. A refresh is given at most
  [REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS], whatever this says.
@param messages The app's messages by error code; codes it lacks use English.
@param sessionProfile The session profile to ask for, where the environment lets a client
  choose one.
@param passkeys The system's passkey sheet. `null` (the default) means this client has no
  passkey call that works: each answers `passkey.unsupported` before any request.
@param google Google's own sheet. `null` means [signInWithGoogle] answers
  `provider.unsupported` before any request.
@param browser The browser a provider sign-in is shown in. `null` means [signIn] with a
  provider answers `provider.unsupported` before any request.
@param deviceKeys Where the device's key is kept. `null` means no session of this client is
  bound to a key and no request carries a proof. With one, the six calls that start an
  attempt and every refresh carry a proof.
@throws IllegalArgumentException for options that can never work. Its message never repeats
  a value it was given.

```kotlin
class TulaClient internal constructor(
    publishableKey: String,
    baseUrl: String,
    storage: TokenStorage,
    http: HttpEngine,
    clock: Clock,
    timeoutMs: Long,
```

#### `TulaClient.signIn`

_fun_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/TulaClient.kt`

Sign in with a provider through the browser: starts the attempt, opens the provider's
page, and exchanges the ticket the API sends the browser back with.

What the browser returns is read only when it is [redirectUrl], character for
character, followed by `#`. The binding the start was given is kept in memory and
nowhere else.

@param provider The provider.
@param redirectUrl Where the API sends the browser back to: an app link, or a custom
  scheme of the app for a provider that binds its code with PKCE. One of the
  environment's allowed redirect URLs; the server judges it, never the client.
@return What became of it. A closed browser is [ProviderOutcome.Cancelled].
@throws TulaError `provider.unsupported` without a browser and `flow.busy` while
  another sheet of the client is out, both before any request;
  `request.redirect_not_allowed`, `auth.method_disabled` as the API answered them;
  `network.failed`, `network.timeout`, `rate_limited` for an exchange that got no
  answer: the ticket is kept for a minute and [retryProviderSignIn] presents it again.

```kotlin
suspend fun signIn(provider: OAuthProvider, redirectUrl: String): ProviderOutcome
```

_fun_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/TulaClient.kt`

A usable access token: the one in memory while it is fresh, a new one otherwise. Calls

#### `TulaSession.signOut`

_fun_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/TulaClient.kt`

Sign out: here first, then on the server.

**A failed sign-out is not a sign-out.** When the server could not be told (or the
stored token could not be removed) this throws: the client is signed out, the session
may still be alive on the server, and calling it again tells the server. Navigate away
only after a call that returned.

@throws TulaError `network.failed`, `network.timeout`, `storage.failed` or what the API
  answered.

```kotlin
suspend fun signOut(): Unit
```

### `TulaAuthState`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-ui/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/ui/TulaAuthModel.kt`

Everything a screen draws from, at one moment. A new value is published for every change.

**It can hold a password or a code** ([password], [code], [newPassword]) while their screen is
open, so it prints as its type's name and nothing else. Never log one, never put one in a
`Bundle`, a `SavedStateHandle` or `rememberSaveable`.

```kotlin
data class TulaAuthState(
    /** The screen to draw. */
    val screen: TulaAuthScreen,
    /** The address field. */
    val email: String = "",
    /** The password field of a sign-in or a sign-up. Emptied when its screen is left. */
    val password: String = "",
    /** The code field. Emptied when its screen is left. */
    val code: String = "",
    /** The new-password field. Emptied when its screen is left. */
    val newPassword: String = "",
    /** Whether an action is being sent. A second one is not started meanwhile. */
    val isPending: Boolean = false,
    /** What went wrong that is not about one field, in the table's words. */
    val formError: String? = null,
    /** What is wrong with each field, in the table's words. */
    val fieldErrors: Map<TulaAuthField, List<String>> = emptyMap(),
    /** Something that went right, in words: "A new code is on its way." */
    val status: String? = null,
    /** Where the focus was last asked to go. */
    val focus: TulaAuthFocus = TulaAuthFocus.Title,
    /** Counts the requests to move the focus: a screen moves it when this changes. */
    val focusRequests: Int = 0,
    /** The environment's app name, once [TulaAuthModel.loadConfig] has read it. */
    val appName: String? = null,
    /** Whether a sign-up may leave the password out (`signUp.password: optional`). */
    val passwordOptional: Boolean = false,
    /** The secret fields whose text is drawn in the clear ("show password"). */
    val revealed: Set<TulaAuthField> = emptySet(),
)
```

### `TulaAuthModel`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-ui/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/ui/TulaAuthModel.kt`

What is behind the screens: which one is drawn, what the fields hold, what went wrong, and
the actions of the buttons. A composable draws [state] and calls [perform]; it decides
nothing. The model has no Compose and no Android in it, so all of it is tested on the JVM.

**It holds no token.** A password and a code are in [state] only while their screen is open:
every change of screen, the completion and [close] empty all three. It prints as its type's
name, and nothing it holds is logged.

**A flow that is left is discarded** ([Flow.discard]): by [close], by going to another flow
and by starting again. An answer that arrives afterwards changes nothing here and signs
nobody in. A flow that had already completed when it was left is not one of those: it cannot
be discarded (the client is signed in), so its answer is shown and reported like any other
completion.

**No action is silent.** A button of the open screen does what it says, marks what is
missing, says what went wrong, or, where its flow is gone, lands on the start of the flow
with words. An action the open screen does not offer does nothing.

It may be called from any thread: every change is made under one lock, and never across a
suspension. [announce] and [onSignedIn] are called outside that lock, on the thread whose
call made the change.

@param client The app's client.
@param mode The flow to open on.
@param strings The strings.
@param announce Says a message to a screen reader. The screens pass the platform's; a test
  passes its own.
@param onSignedIn Called once for each flow that completed, when the client is signed in:
  also when the flow's screen was left or closed meanwhile (so it can be called after
  [close]), and also when the session could not be stored.

```kotlin
class TulaAuthModel(
    private val client: TulaClient,
    mode: TulaAuthMode = TulaAuthMode.SIGN_IN,
    strings: TulaStrings = TulaStrings(),
    private val announce: (String) -> Unit = {},
    private val onSignedIn: (() -> Unit)? = null,
)
```

The screen is closing: discard the flow, forget what every field held, the address

buttons that can do nothing. It closes onto the start of its own mode also when what was

### `TulaStrings`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-ui/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/ui/TulaStrings.kt`

Every string the screens show: one table, in English by default.

An app translates, or rewords, by copying the table with the properties it wants and handing
it to the screens:

```kotlin
val strings = TulaStrings(
    signInTitle = "Welcome back",
    errors = mapOf("auth.invalid_credentials" to "That did not match. Try again."),
)
```

A value in `{braces}` is filled in by the screens (`{appName}`, `{destination}`, `{time}`,
`{label}`, `{message}`); a string that leaves one out simply does not show it. Every string
is drawn as text: nothing here is parsed as HTML, Markdown or a link.

**A server's error is shown by its code, never by the server's own words.** The message of a
code is `errors[code]` when the table has one, otherwise the contract's English sentence for
a code this version knows, otherwise [unknownError]: text a server wrote is never put on the
screen. The client's own `messages` table is not read by the screens: a translation of an
error goes in [errors].

It is a Kotlin table and not Android string resources on purpose: the model that words a
problem runs on the JVM with no `Context`, where it is tested, and an app that keeps its
translations in `strings.xml` builds this table from them (`stringResource`) in one place.

```kotlin
data class TulaStrings(
    /** Said of a button whose action is being sent. */
    val loading: String = "Loading…",
    /** Under a field that was left empty. */
    val required: String = "This field is required.",
    /** Goes back to the screen before. */
    val back: String = "Back",
    /** The last line of every screen. */
    val securedBy: String = "Secured by Tula",
    /**
     * What a field is read as, by a screen reader, when it has a problem. `{label}` is the
     * field's label and `{message}` its problems.
     */
    val fieldInvalid: String = "{label}, invalid: {message}",
    /**
     * What a problem starts with, so that it is one in words and not only in colour.
     * `{message}` is the problem.
     */
    val errorPrefix: String = "Error: {message}",
    /** After a `rate_limited` answer that says how long to wait. `{time}` is the wait. */
    val retryIn: String = "Try again in {time}.",
    /** A wait under a minute. `{seconds}` is the number. */
    val seconds: String = "{seconds}s",
    /** A wait of a minute or more. */
    val minutesSeconds: String = "{minutes}m {seconds}s",
    /** The title of the screen a sign-in starts on. */
    val signInTitle: String = "Sign in",
    /** `{appName}` is the environment's app name. */
    val signInSubtitle: String = "to continue to {appName}",
    /** The subtitle while, or where, the app's name is not known. */
    val signInSubtitleNoApp: String = "Welcome back",
    /** The label of the address field, on every screen that has one. */
    val emailLabel: String = "Email address",
    /** The button that starts a sign-in or a sign-up. */
    val continueButton: String = "Continue",
    /** The title of the password step. */
    val passwordTitle: String = "Enter your password",
    /** The label of the password field. */
    val passwordLabel: String = "Password",
    /** The button that sends the password. */
    val signInSubmit: String = "Sign in",
    /** The link from a sign-in to a password reset. */
    val forgotPassword: String = "Forgot password?",
    /** Beside the address a sign-in is for: goes back to change it. */
    val changeEmail: String = "Change",
    /** What the address a sign-in is for is read as. `{email}` is the address. */
    val signingInAs: String = "Signing in as {email}",
    /** The words before the link to the sign-up. */
    val noAccount: String = "New here?",
    /** The link from a sign-in to a sign-up. */
    val signUpLink: String = "Create an account",
    /** Said, and shown, when a flow has signed somebody in. */
    val signedIn: String = "You are signed in.",
    /** The link from the emailed code back to the password. */
    val usePassword: String = "Use your password",
    /** The button, and the link, that asks for an emailed sign-in code. */
    val emailCode: String = "Email me a code",
    /** The title of the emailed sign-in code's screens. */
    val emailCodeTitle: String = "Check your email",
    /** Under the title, before the code was asked for. */
    val emailCodePrompt: String = "We will email you a 6-digit code to sign in with.",
    /** `{destination}` is the masked address the server sent the code to. */
    val emailCodeSubtitle: String = "Enter the 6-digit code we sent to {destination}.",
    /** The link that asks for another sign-in email. */
    val emailResend: String = "Send a new email",
    /** Said, and shown, once another sign-in email was asked for. */
    val emailResent: String = "A new email is on its way.",
    /** The title of the screen a sign-up starts on. */
    val signUpTitle: String = "Create your account",
    /** Under the sign-up's title. */
    val signUpSubtitle: String = "Welcome! Sign up to get started.",
    /** The password field's label where the environment lets a sign-up go without one. */
    val passwordOptionalLabel: String = "Password (optional)",
    /** Under that field: what leaving it empty means. */
    val passwordOptionalHint: String = "Leave it empty to sign in with a code we email you instead.",
    /** The words before the link to the sign-in. */
    val haveAccount: String = "Already have an account?",
    /** The link from a sign-up to a sign-in. */
    val signInLink: String = "Sign in",
    /** The title of the step that verifies an address. */
    val verificationTitle: String = "Check your email",
    /** `{destination}` is the masked address the server sent the code to. */
    val verificationSubtitle: String = "Enter the 6-digit code we sent to {destination}.",
    /** The label of the code field. */
    val codeLabel: String = "Verification code",
    /** Under the code field: what a code looks like. */
    val codeHint: String = "6 digits",
    /** Under the code field when it holds fewer than six digits. */
    val codeIncomplete: String = "Enter the 6-digit code.",
    /** The button that sends the code. */
    val verifySubmit: String = "Verify",
    /** The link that asks for another code. */
    val resend: String = "Resend code",
    /** Said, and shown, once another code was asked for. */
    val resent: String = "A new code is on its way.",
    /** The title of the screen a reset starts on. */
    val resetTitle: String = "Reset your password",
    /** Under the reset's title. */
    val resetSubtitle: String = "Enter your email address and we will send you a code.",
    /** The button that starts a reset. */
    val sendCode: String = "Send code",
    /** The title of the step that takes the code and the new password. */
    val newPasswordTitle: String = "Choose a new password",
    /** `{destination}` is the masked address the server sent the code to. */
    val newPasswordSubtitle: String =
        "Enter the 6-digit code we sent to {destination} and a new password.",
    /** The label of a new password's field. */
    val newPasswordLabel: String = "New password",
    /** The button that sends the code and the new password. */
    val resetSubmit: String = "Reset password",
    /** The link from a reset back to the sign-in. */
    val backToSignIn: String = "Back to sign in",
    /** The title of the last step of a sign-in whose password is too old. */
    val expiredPasswordTitle: String = "Your password has expired",
    /** Under that title. */
    val expiredPasswordSubtitle: String = "Choose a new password to finish signing in.",
    /** The button that stores the new password and finishes the sign-in. */
    val expiredPasswordSubmit: String = "Save password and sign in",
    /** What the button in a password field says while the password is hidden. */
    val showPassword: String = "Show password",
    /** What it says while the password is shown. */
    val hidePassword: String = "Hide password",
    /** The title of the screen for a step this version cannot continue. */
    val notSupportedTitle: String = "This step is not supported",
    /** Under that title: what a person can do. */
    val notSupportedMessage: String =
        "This version of the app cannot continue this sign-in. Update the app, or sign in another way.",
    /** The button that discards the attempt and goes back to the first screen. */
    val startAgain: String = "Start again",
    /** Above the first screen, when a button found that its attempt was no longer open. */
    val flowLost: String = "That attempt is no longer open. Start again.",
    /**
     * On the signed-in screen, when the flow completed and the session could not be stored
     * (`storage.failed`): the client is signed in for as long as the app runs. "May", because
     * a later refresh that succeeds stores the session after all.
     */
    val sessionNotSaved: String =
        "Your session could not be saved on this device. You may be signed out when the app closes.",
    /**
     * Messages by error code (`auth.invalid_credentials`, `network.failed`), for a translation
     * or another wording. A code that is not here gets the contract's English sentence.
     */
    val errors: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
    /**
     * The message of a code this version does not know. The server's own words for such a code
     * are never shown.
     */
    val unknownError: String = "Something went wrong. Try again.",
)
```

### `TulaThemeGrammar`

_object_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-ui/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/ui/TulaThemeValues.kt`

The contract's grammar of theme values (`isValidThemeValue` in `@tula/contract/theme`).

It is never looser than the contract's: what that refuses, this refuses. It is stricter in
one place, on purpose: a value that holds anything outside ASCII is refused (the contract
allows Unicode white space between the parts of a value, and nothing else outside ASCII).

It is a copy kept equal by hand, and held to `packages/contract/src/theme-cases.json` by a
test: a rule changed in `theme.ts` is changed here in the same change.

```kotlin
object TulaThemeGrammar
```

### `TulaResolvedTheme`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-ui/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/ui/TulaThemeValues.kt`

A theme with every value checked and turned into what the platform draws with.

```kotlin
val theme = TulaThemeDefaults.theme.let {
    it.copy(light = it.light.copy(primary = "#0f766e"), dark = it.dark.copy(primary = "#5eead4"))
}
val resolved = TulaResolvedTheme.of(theme)
resolved.refused   // [] — or the tokens whose value was not used, e.g. ["light.primary"]
```

A value that is refused (by the contract's grammar, or because this version cannot draw it)
is replaced by the default theme's value for that token. Nothing an app or a tenant wrote
reaches a screen any other way.

```kotlin
@ConsistentCopyVisibility
data class TulaResolvedTheme internal constructor(
    /** The light scheme. */
    val light: TulaResolvedScheme,
    /** The dark scheme. */
    val dark: TulaResolvedScheme,
    /** Corner radius of fields and buttons, in density-independent pixels. */
    val radius: Double,
    /** Corner radius of small parts, in density-independent pixels. */
    val radiusSmall: Double,
    /** The typeface of everything. */
    val fontFamily: TulaFontFamily,
    /** The typeface of codes. */
    val fontFamilyMono: TulaFontFamily,
    /** Body text size, in scale-independent pixels: the user's font scale applies. */
    val fontSize: Double,
    /** Size of hints, in scale-independent pixels. */
    val fontSizeSmall: Double,
    /** Size of a title, in scale-independent pixels. */
    val fontSizeTitle: Double,
    /** The spacing unit, in density-independent pixels. */
    val spacing: Double,
    /**
     * The tokens whose value was refused and replaced by the default: `light.primary`,
     * `radius`. A token's key, never the value it was given.
     */
    val refused: List<String>,
)
```

## `tula-auth-compose`

`import dev.tula.auth.compose.*`, from `native/android/tula-auth-compose/src/main/kotlin`.

### `TulaAuth`

_fun_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-compose/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/compose/TulaAuth.kt`

Sign-in, sign-up, email verification and password reset: one screen per step the server
answers, drawn from the app's client.

```kotlin
val state by client.state.collectAsState()
if (state is AuthState.SignedIn) Home() else TulaAuth(client, onSignedIn = { /* navigate */ })
```

The composable makes its own [TulaAuthModel] and keeps it with plain `remember`: nothing that
is typed is put in `rememberSaveable`, a `SavedStateHandle` or a `Bundle`. **When it leaves
the composition the open flow is discarded and every field is emptied**, so an activity that
is recreated (a rotation the manifest does not handle) starts the screen again. An app that
wants an attempt to live through that hoists the model with [TulaAuth]'s other form.

Where the app goes after a sign-in is [onSignedIn] and nothing else: the screens read no
address from an intent or from the server.

`FLAG_SECURE` (no screenshot, nothing in the recents list) is a window's, and so the app's to
set on its activity; the screens do not set it.

@param client The app's client.
@param modifier The modifier of the whole screen.
@param mode The flow to open on.
@param strings Every string the screens show.
@param theme The theme: the generated defaults with what the app, or a tenant, changed. A
  value that is refused is replaced by the default's and never drawn.
@param slots The parts of a screen the app draws itself.
@param onSignedIn Called once for each flow that completed, on the main thread: also when
  the session could not be stored, and also after the screen has left the composition if the
  flow had already completed by then.

```kotlin
@Composable
fun TulaAuth(
    client: TulaClient,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    mode: TulaAuthMode = TulaAuthMode.SIGN_IN,
    strings: TulaStrings = TulaStrings(),
    theme: TulaTheme = TulaThemeDefaults.theme,
    slots: TulaAuthSlots = TulaAuthSlots(),
    onSignedIn: (() -> Unit)? = null,
)
```

### `TulaAuth`

_fun_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-compose/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/compose/TulaAuth.kt`

The same screens over a model the app keeps: in a `ViewModel` (without a `SavedStateHandle`),
for an attempt that lives through a recreated activity.

**The owner closes the model** ([TulaAuthModel.close]) when the screens are left for good:
this form does not, because it cannot tell a rotation from a way out. Until then the model
holds what was typed.

### `TulaAuthSlots`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-compose/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/compose/TulaAuthSlots.kt`

The parts of a screen an app may draw itself. Each has a default, so an app replaces only
what it wants:

```kotlin
TulaAuth(
    client = client,
    slots = TulaAuthSlots(
        header = { header ->
            Image(painterResource(R.drawable.logo), contentDescription = null)
            TulaAuthDefaults.Header(header)
        },
        footer = {},
    ),
)
```

The fields, the links and the problems are not slots: what is typed, how a problem is
associated with its field and how it is said belong to the screens.

A slot is handed words, a theme and a callback, and nothing that is typed: no password and
no code reaches one.

@param header The title and what is under it.
@param primaryButton The screen's main button.
@param footer The last line.

```kotlin
@Immutable
class TulaAuthSlots(
    val header: @Composable (TulaAuthHeader) -> Unit = { TulaAuthDefaults.Header(it) },
    val primaryButton: @Composable (TulaAuthButton) -> Unit = { TulaAuthDefaults.PrimaryButton(it) },
    val footer: @Composable (TulaAuthFooter) -> Unit = { TulaAuthDefaults.Footer(it) },
)
```

## `tula-auth-android`

`import dev.tula.auth.android.*`, from `native/android/tula-auth-android/src/main/kotlin`.

### `CredentialManagerPasskeySheet`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-android/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/android/CredentialManagerSheets.kt`

The passkey sheet of Android's Credential Manager.

The options the server sent are handed over as JSON and the credential comes back as JSON;
neither is kept, logged or put in an error. A sheet the user put away is
[SheetFailure.DISMISSED], which the client reports as a dismissal and not as an error:
that is Credential Manager's own cancellation exception and nothing else. A WebAuthn
`NotAllowedError` is [SheetFailure.FAILED] until a device has shown it means a cancel. A
request that finds no passkey on the device is [SheetFailure.FAILED]: Credential Manager
reports it apart from a dismissal, and nothing was shown that a user put away.

The server accepts a response only from an app the environment's operator registered
(its package name and the SHA-256 fingerprint of its signing certificate), and the device
shows a passkey of the relying party only when that domain's `assetlinks.json` names the
app: see `docs/native-apps.md`.

This class is compiled and linted, and was not run on a device or an emulator.

@param activity The activity the sheet is shown over, asked for at each ceremony so that
  none is held; `null` (no activity is in front) is [SheetFailure.FAILED].

```kotlin
class CredentialManagerPasskeySheet(private val activity: () -> Activity?) : PasskeySheet
```

### `CredentialManagerGoogleSheet`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-android/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/android/CredentialManagerSheets.kt`

Google's account sheet through Credential Manager, for a sign-in with Google's ID token.

The sheet is given the server's nonce as it is and the ID token it answers is returned to
the client, which exchanges it; the token is kept nowhere. Every account on the device is
offered, not only one that signed in to this app before.

This class is compiled and linted, and was not run on a device or an emulator.

@param serverClientId The OAuth client id of type "Web application" of the app's Google
  project: the audience of the token. The environment's Google provider has it as its
  client id, or lists the app's Android client id among its additional client ids.
@param activity The activity the sheet is shown over, asked for at each ceremony so that
  none is held; `null` is [SheetFailure.FAILED].

```kotlin
class CredentialManagerGoogleSheet(
    private val serverClientId: String,
    private val activity: () -> Activity?,
) : GoogleSheet
```

### `CustomTabsBrowserSession`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-android/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/android/CustomTabsBrowserSession.kt`

A provider's sign-in page in a Custom Tab of the user's browser, and the address the app
is opened with afterwards.

The page is opened in the user's browser, never in a web view of the app: the provider's
password is typed where the app cannot read it. The browser comes back by opening the app
with the redirect URL, an app link or a custom scheme the app declares in its manifest, and
the app hands that address over:

- the activity that receives the redirect calls [returned] with the intent it was opened
  with (`onNewIntent`, or `onCreate` for an activity of its own);
- the activity that asked calls [resumed] from `onResume`: coming back to the front with
  no redirect is the user closing the tab, which is a cancelled sign-in and not an error.

A platform opens an app with whatever matches its filter, and anybody can open an app with
a URL. So [returned] takes an address for the browser's return only when it is the redirect
URL the sign-in asked for, character for character, followed by `#` (the rule is
[BrowserReturn]'s, in the JVM module, where it is tested); any other intent is the app's
own and leaves a waiting sign-in waiting. The address is then passed on as it is, and the
client reads it by the same rule before any request.

This class is compiled and linted, and was not run on a device or an emulator.

@param activity The activity the tab is opened from, asked for at each sign-in so that
  none is held; `null` is [SheetFailure.FAILED].

```kotlin
class CustomTabsBrowserSession(private val activity: () -> Activity?) : BrowserSession
```

_fun_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-android/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/android/CustomTabsBrowserSession.kt`

Hand over the intent the app was opened with. Every intent may be handed over: one
that is not the return is left to the app.

@param intent The intent of `onNewIntent` or `onCreate`.
@return `true` only when a sign-in was waiting and the intent's address is the
  redirect URL that sign-in asked for, character for character, followed by `#`: the
  sign-in then has it. `false` means the intent is the app's own to handle, and a
  waiting sign-in still waits. A return to the redirect URL with no fragment is
  `false` too: it carries no answer, and the sign-in ends as cancelled at [resumed].

The alias of the device key in the Android Keystore, unless the app names another.

### `KeystoreDeviceKeyStore`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-android/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/android/KeystoreDeviceKeyStore.kt`

The device key of a bound session, in the Android Keystore.

A P-256 key pair that signs and does nothing else. The Keystore gives no call that exports
a private key it made, so the key is non-exportable by the platform's API; the store asks
for StrongBox first and, where the device says it has none, makes the key in the Keystore's
default implementation. Which of the two a device used is not recorded, and the server is
told neither: binding proves a key signed, not where it lives.

[existing] answers `null` only when the Keystore says it has no entry under the alias;
every other failure is thrown, because the client ends a session only for a key it knows
is gone. This store never throws `DeviceKeyUnusableException`: no Keystore exception is
documented to mean that a key that needs no user authentication can never be used again.
An app that decides so signs out and calls `TulaClient.removeDeviceKey()`.

This class is compiled and linted, and was not run on a device or an emulator.

@param alias The Keystore alias of the key.

```kotlin
class KeystoreDeviceKeyStore(private val alias: String = DEFAULT_DEVICE_KEY_ALIAS) : DeviceKeyStore
```

### `KeystoreTokenStorage`

_class_, defined in `native/android/tula-auth-android/src/main/kotlin/dev/tula/auth/android/KeystoreTokenStorage.kt`

The [TokenStorage] for a device: the refresh token sealed with an AES-256-GCM key that is
made in the Android Keystore and never leaves it, and only the sealed value written to the
app's private preferences.

```kotlin
val tula = TulaClient(
    publishableKey = "tula_pk_…",
    baseUrl = "https://auth.example.com",
    storage = KeystoreTokenStorage(applicationContext),
)
```

The key asks for no user authentication (a refresh in the background must work while the
device is locked) and is not exportable, so a backup of the preferences file holds a value
no other device can open. Where the device has no key, such a value is read as "no token"
and removed. Where a key exists and the value's authentication tag fails, the storage
**throws**: the client reports `storage.failed`, keeps the session it has and deletes
nothing; the entry goes when the user signs out or signs in again.

Android's Auto Backup and device transfer copy the preferences file unless the app
excludes it; `docs/kotlin.md` has the two rules to add, naming [DEFAULT_PREFERENCES_NAME].

@param context Any context; the application's is what is kept.
@param keyAlias The Keystore alias of the sealing key.
@param preferencesName The preferences file of the sealed values.

```kotlin
class KeystoreTokenStorage(
    context: Context,
    keyAlias: String = DEFAULT_KEY_ALIAS,
    preferencesName: String = DEFAULT_PREFERENCES_NAME,
) : TokenStorage by SealedTokenStorage(
    AndroidKeystoreSealer(keyAlias),
    PreferenceEntries(
        context.applicationContext.getSharedPreferences(preferencesName, Context.MODE_PRIVATE),
    ),
)
```
